docs.title: Main page
docs.text:
The reference for NEOTOKYO Rebuild, a tactical first-person shooter rebuilt on the 2025 Source SDK. Every stat here is extracted from the game's source code and linked to the exact line it came from.

29 weapons & items · 3 classes · 3 game modes · 32 official maps. Plus VIP and Juggernaut, two modes still in development.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: NT;RE plays differently from most shooters. These are the mechanics that decide fights, each with a link to the full detail.

docs.title: 1. You get one life per round
docs.text: In Capture the Ghost, the main mode, you don't respawn until the next round. A round is about 3 minutes of play after a 15-second freeze. Rounds end on a ghost capture or when one team is wiped out. If time runs out it's a draw, whoever holds the ghost.

docs.title: 2. Headshots aren't special
docs.text: Head and chest both take ×1.0 damage; stomach and arms ×0.75; legs ×0.6. Aim at centre mass. There's no damage falloff over distance, and every bullet does ×1.485 its listed base damage. See Damage & penetration.

docs.title: 3. Your class decides how you fight
docs.text: Class Play it as Key trait Recon Scout, flanker Free sprint, 13 s cloak, super jump; only 100 HP Assault Rifleman Motion vision spots moving cloakers; widest gun choice Support Anchor, suppression 225 HP, thermal sees through smoke; can't sprint or cloak

docs.title: 4. XP unlocks weapons
docs.text: Kills (+1), assists (+1) and round wins (+1) raise your rank, which unlocks better primaries. Teamkills and suicides cost 1 XP. A ghost capture jumps every surviving teammate straight to the next rank, which is worth far more than a few kills. XP resets at the start of every match. See Loadouts & ranks.

docs.title: 5. Watch what's in your hands
docs.text: Your movement speed depends on the weapon you're holding, from ×1.0 down to ×0.675 for the PZ252. Switch to your sidearm or knife (×0.85) to rotate faster. See Movement.

docs.title: 6. Cloak isn't invisibility
docs.text: Thermoptic camo is hard to see when you're still, but Assault motion vision highlights you the moment you move. Firing an unsuppressed weapon makes you flash, and so does switching the cloak on. Suppressed weapons keep you hidden.

docs.title: 7. Don't shoot teammates early
docs.text: Friendly fire is on. During the first 7 seconds of each round, damage to teammates is reflected back to you at double strength. See Team damage.

docs.title: About this wiki
docs.text: This is a prototype of a wiki for NEOTOKYO Rebuild (NT;RE), built with MkDocs and the Material theme. It exists to settle structure, page types and visual design. An earlier static HTML prototype lives alongside it in prototype/ for comparison.

docs.title: How the numbers are sourced
docs.text:
Every stat on this site was extracted from the NeotokyoRebuild/neo repository: weapon scripts in game/neo/scripts/ and the C++ gameplay code in src/game/. Each number carries a footnote that links to the exact file and line it came from, pinned to a specific commit (see the page footer).

When the game changes, the data can be re-extracted and every page rebuilt. Tables and stat blocks are generated from the data at build time, so no number is typed by hand twice.

docs.title: Page types demonstrated
docs.text:
• Hub pages: Main page, Weapons, Classes, Game modes
  • Weapon pages: one Markdown file per weapon, in a fixed layout (overview, general stats, damage, shots to kill, time to kill, handling, availability). The prose is hand-editable; every number comes from a {{weapon:…}} snippet.
  • Mechanic articles: hand-written explanations with citations, such as Thermoptic camouflage and Damage & penetration
  • Reference tables: Console variables, Maps, Loadouts & ranks

docs.title: Not in the prototype
docs.text:
• Editing and page history: pages are Markdown files in the repository
  • Images: grey boxes mark where screenshots or renders would go, pending a decision on asset licensing
  • Lore and story content: this pass covers gameplay mechanics and stats only
  • Terminology and external resources pages

docs.title: Build
docs.text: In wiki/, install the requirements (pip install -r requirements.txt) and run mkdocs serve. Pages live in docs/, extracted game data in data/, and the snippets, wiki links and citations are handled by hooks/ntre.py and hooks/generators.py. See Style guide for the markup.

docs.title: Style guide
docs.text: The rules every page on this wiki follows. The guide is part of the prototype's source and changes in the same commit as the style it describes, so it always matches the pages around it.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
• Plain and direct. Address the player as you, in the present tense.
  • Open with what the thing is and why it matters. Name the subject in bold in the first sentence.
  • One idea per sentence. Cut filler, hype and hedging that carries no information.
  • British spelling (colour, armour, behaviour). Code identifiers and quoted strings keep their own spelling.
  • Headings in sentence case: Weapon speed scale, not Weapon Speed Scale.

docs.title: Facts and sources
docs.text:
• Every gameplay number cites the line it comes from: [[src:path:line]] becomes a footnote linked to GitHub at the pinned commit.
  • Never guess. If the code is ambiguous, or client and server disagree, say so in an amber callout labelled Unconfirmed, Unverified or Unresolved.
  • Say how a claim was established: "inferred from the code" is different from "tested in game".
  • Tables and infoboxes take their numbers from the extracted data, not from hand-typed copies.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
• Weapons use their in-game display names: MPN45, SRM-S, ZR68-L, Murata Supa-7, MilSO, BALC.
  • Classes are capitalised: Recon, Assault, Support, VIP, Juggernaut.
  • Game modes take the full name first, then the code: Capture the Ghost (CTG).
  • Teams: Jinrai and NSF. The objective is the ghost, lowercase in running text.
  • Console variables and file names go in code, with their default where it matters: mp_friendlyfire 1.

docs.title: Page anatomy
docs.text:
1. A # Title, and a one-line description in the front matter
  2. A lead paragraph that stands on its own
  3. An infobox for classes, modes and mechanics with stats
  4. Sections under ## headings. The contents list on the right is automatic.
  5. The generated references, last

Weapon pages follow one layout, in this order: Overview, General stats, Damage, Shots to kill, Time to kill, Handling, then anything weapon-specific (bolt action, heat), Availability, Suppressor and Technical notes. The prose is yours to write; the numbers come from {{weapon:…}} snippets, which read the weapon named in the front matter (weapon: weapon_zr68s).

  • Comparisons go in tables, not lists. Numbers are right-aligned in monospace.
  • Hit locations with the same multiplier share a column: head / chest, stomach / arms, legs.
  • Link a page's first mention in each section, not every mention. Write [[slug|Label]]; a slug is the file name without .md, or the folder name for an index.md.
  • Page addresses follow the menu: /weapons/rifles/zr68-s/. Folders and file names are lowercase with hyphens, and every slug is unique across the wiki.
  • Callouts (!!! info "Label") have a short label. Neutral callouts are for notes; amber warning ones are for anything quirky, unverified or in progress.

docs.title: Work-in-progress modes
docs.text:
• VIP and Juggernaut are still in development. Stat lists keep them, but last, greyed out and tagged WIP. This includes their weapons, the SMAC and BALC.
  • Headline counts leave them out: the main page says 3 classes and 3 game modes, with a note naming the two in development.
  • Their own pages, and their weapons' pages, open with an amber Work in progress callout.

docs.title: Visual
docs.text:
• Dark by default, minimal, neutral, with a light theme one click away. Hairline borders; no shadows, gradients or emoji.
  • Blocks are rounded: 8px on tables, callouts, cards, infoboxes, code and the search box; 6px on navigation items.
  • Red is for the brand dot only: after page titles and beside the current page. Never for link text, because red text means a missing page.
  • Link underlines are a cool, desaturated cyan. On hover the line fills left to right, snaps into place, pulses once and settles. Cards lift to a lighter surface on hover instead.
  • The NT;RE mark is the primary logo. The wordmark appears only on the main page.
  • Image slots are grey placeholders labelled with what belongs there, until assets are licensed.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
Every player in NT;RE picks one of three classes: Recon, Assault or Support. The class sets your health, movement speed, vision mode, whether you can cloak, and which primary weapons you can choose from at each rank. Two more roles, VIP and Juggernaut, can't be picked from the menu. Their game modes assign them, and both modes are still in development.

The two teams, Jinrai and NSF, have no gameplay differences. They differ only in player models, HUD colour and which spawn they start from.

docs.title: Choosing and changing class
docs.text:
Class changes apply immediately while you are dead, during the pre-round freeze (before you fire or drop a weapon), during warmup, or in DM/TDM within 10 seconds of spawning. At any other time the change is queued for your next spawn.31

Servers can cap or ban classes with sv_neo_class_limit_recon, sv_neo_class_limit_assault and sv_neo_class_limit_support (default -1, unlimited; 0 bans the class). If the class you ask for is full, you get the first class that isn't.3233

docs.title: Shared rules
docs.text:
• No armour. Health is the only durability stat; no class has damage reduction.34
  • Speed depends on the weapon in hand. Every weapon multiplies your class speed by 0.675–1.0. See Movement.
  • A knife backstab kills any class. It deals exactly 226 damage, one more than Support's maximum health.35
  • No prone. Stand, crouch and lean are the only stances.

The Assault is the middle class. It has more health than Recon, a short cloak, motion vision that picks out anything that moves, and the largest primary weapon selection in the game, from SMGs up to the SRS sniper rifle and AA13 auto-shotgun.

docs.title: Strengths and weaknesses
docs.text:
• Biggest sprint multiplier. Sprint is ×1.6 of run speed (160 → 256 u/s), against Recon's ×1.35. Recon still sprints faster in absolute terms (270).14
  • Sprint costs AUX. 5 AUX per second while moving, so a full bar lasts 20 seconds. AUX does not regenerate while sprinting, and every time you stop sprinting another 0.5 AUX is taken.15
  • Short cloak. 8 seconds, recharging at 0.25/s, so 32 s from empty to full.16
  • Spawns with a grenade, along with the Tachi pistol and knife.13
  • 1.15-second slowdown after landing a jump, like every class except Recon.

docs.title: Motion vision
docs.text: Any model moving faster than 0.5 u/s is drawn with an extra highlight pass, and that includes cloaked players. A cloaked enemy who stands perfectly still disappears again.17 See Vision modes.

The Recon is NT;RE's scout. It has the highest base speed, the longest thermoptic camouflage, a sprint that costs no AUX, and a super jump. In exchange it has the lowest health of the three selectable classes and the narrowest choice of primary weapons.

docs.title: Strengths and weaknesses
docs.text:
• Fastest class. Runs at 2002 u/s and sprints at 27034 u/s, against 160/256 for Assault.
  • Free sprint. Sprinting does not drain AUX, and AUX keeps recharging at 2.5/s while you sprint.15 AUX is only spent on the super jump.
  • No landing penalty. Every other class slows down for 1.15 s after a jump. Recon doesn't.16
  • Highest jump: 54 units, 1.5× the default.17
  • Fragile. 100 HP, the joint lowest with the VIP.

docs.title: Super jump
docs.text:
Hold Sprint and press Jump while moving forward or backward. It adds a horizontal boost equal to your current maximum speed on top of a normal jump, and costs 45 AUX.1819

The jump only fires if all of these are true:20

  • You are sprinting, on the ground, and not standing in water above your feet
  • You are not carrying the ghost
  • You have at least 45 AUX

Quirk

The code takes the 45 AUX whenever those conditions pass, but only applies the boost if exactly one of forward or back is held. A sprint-jump with only strafe keys held costs 45 AUX and gives no boost. Holding a strafe key alongside forward cuts the boost to ×0.707.21 This is inferred from the code and has not been confirmed in play.

The boost follows your view direction with the vertical part removed but not renormalised, so looking up or down shrinks it by the cosine of your pitch. Super jump at eye level for maximum distance.22

docs.title: Thermoptic camouflage
docs.text: Recon has a 13-second cloak that recharges at 0.55 per second (about 23.6 s from empty to full), against Assault's 8 s at 0.25/s.23 See Thermoptic camouflage for what reveals a cloaked player.

docs.title: Night vision
docs.text: Recon uses night vision, a full-screen brightening filter. It doesn't highlight anything specific, unlike motion or thermal vision.

The Support is the heavy class. With 225 HP it can take almost twice the punishment of an Assault. It sees uncloaked players as hot silhouettes through thermal vision, even through smoke, and is the only class that can carry the PZ252 machine gun. It cannot sprint and cannot cloak.

docs.title: Strengths and weaknesses
docs.text:
• Highest health of any selectable class: 225.11 There is no armour on top of it. Only a knife backstab (226 damage) is guaranteed to kill outright.12
  • Cannot sprint. A Support sprint speed constant (216) exists in the code but is commented as reserved for future use.1314
  • No AUX use at all, and no thermoptic camouflage.
  • Thermal vision sees through smoke. The smoke screen overlay is switched off while thermal is active.15
  • Biggest target: a 70-unit standing hull, the largest of the selectable classes.

docs.title: Thermal vision and cloak
docs.text: Thermal vision draws uncloaked players, NPCs and corpses as hot. A cloaked player is drawn with their normal material and no thermal highlight, so they don't stand out from the cold background the way you might expect.16

docs.title: Round flow
docs.text:
All the scored modes follow the same cycle:18

  1. Warmup (45 s): runs once when a match starts. Players respawn freely and XP doesn't count.19
  2. Pre-round freeze (15 s): you can look around and change loadout but can't move, and you can't be hurt.20
  3. Live round. The round timer includes the freeze, so a 3.25-minute CTG round has about 3:00 of live play.21
  4. Overtime, where the mode has it.
  5. Post-round (15 s, mp_chattime), then the next freeze.22

When the match leaves warmup, team scores, rounds won and every player's XP reset to 0.23 Spawn sides and capture zones swap between the teams every round.24

A round won't start while either team is empty; it retries every 10 seconds.25 In one-life modes you can still spawn up to 15 s after the freeze ends (sv_neo_latespawn_max_time).26

docs.title: Match length
docs.text:
• The "score limit" counts rounds won, not kills.27
  • With a round limit set, the match ends early once the trailing team can no longer catch up.28
  • If rounds won are tied when the limit is reached, play continues in sudden death until a team wins a round (neo_round_sudden_death 1).29

docs.title: Choosing the mode
docs.text:
By default each map sets its own mode through a neo_game_config entity. A map without one falls back to Free Roam.30 Servers can override this with sv_neo_gamemode_enforcement:

Value Behaviour 0 Mode set by the map (default) 1 Always sv_neo_gamemode_single31 2 Random from the sv_neo_gamemode_random_allow bitmask, without repeats until every allowed mode has been played. The default mask, 11, covers TDM, CTG and DM.32 3 Player vote, using each client's neo_vote_game_mode33

docs.title: Competitive features
docs.text: CTG, VIP and JGR support the competitive extras. sv_neo_comp 1 turns them all on at once: a ready-up lobby (5 players per team by default), .pause/.unpause (60 s or 180 s), spectators limited to their own team, and paired ghost spawns.34

docs.title: Other modes
docs.text:
• Training (TUT): map-scripted tutorials (ntre_class_tut, ntre_shooting_tut) with no round logic. Completing them earns achievements.35
  • Free Roam (EMT): no objective and no scoring. You can change team, class and loadout while alive.17

docs.title: Bots
docs.text: Bots have dedicated behaviour for CTG (seeking, carrying and escorting the ghost, lone-wolf ambushes) and JGR. In TDM, DM and VIP they fall back to generic seek-and-destroy. You can command bots with Use.3637

docs.text:

Capture the Ghost (CTG) is NT;RE's core mode. Each round, an AI core called the ghost spawns somewhere on the map. A team wins the round by carrying it into its capture zone or by wiping out the enemy team. You get one life per round.

docs.title: Winning a round
docs.text:
• Ghost capture: a live player carrying the ghost enters the radius of an active capture zone owned by their team (or a neutral zone) while the round is live. The round is won instantly; there is no hold timer.34
  • Team elimination: the enemy team has 0 living members. If both teams reach 0 at once, the round is a stalemate.5
  • Time runs out with no capture or elimination: stalemate ('TIE'). Neither team gets a round win and nobody gets round-end XP.6
  • Map logic can force a winner through neo_game_config FireTeamWin / FireRoundTie inputs.7

Time-out is always a draw

When the clock runs out it's a stalemate, no matter who holds the ghost or how many players are alive. The code has a "win by numbers" outcome, but nothing triggers it.8

docs.title: Capture zones
docs.text: Capture zones (neo_ghost_retrieval_point) belong to one team or are neutral. The capture registers the instant a living ghost carrier is within the zone's radius; there's no hold timer. Zones are checked 10 times a second, using 3D distance from the zone's centre.15 Zone ownership swaps every round along with the spawns.16

docs.title: Overtime
docs.text: Off by default (sv_neo_ctg_ghost_overtime_enabled 0). When it's on and the ghost is being carried with 10 s or less left, the round can run up to 45 s past the limit while the ghost stays in hand. If the carrier drops it, the time left shrinks back to the 10-second grace.17

docs.title: XP and rewards
docs.text:
A ghost capture is the most valuable thing you can do in NT;RE. Every surviving player on the capturing team is raised straight to the next rank threshold (0 → 4 → 10 → 20).18 Dead teammates get the normal +1.

Winning by elimination gives +1 to the whole team, +1 more to each survivor, and +1 more to the ghost carrier. A surviving carrier therefore gets +3.19 See Loadouts & ranks.

docs.title: Cap prevention
docs.text: If the last living player on a team kills themselves, disconnects or dies to their own team's grenade while the enemy is carrying the ghost, the enemy team still gets the capture reward when it wins the round (sv_neo_suicide_prevent_cap_punish 1).20

The ghost is the objective in Capture the Ghost. Whoever carries it can see every enemy within about 46 metres, but everyone else on the map can see where the carrier is.

docs.title: Picking it up
docs.text:
• It goes in the primary slot. You can't pick it up while holding a primary weapon, so drop yours first.4
  • It can't shoot or aim.5
  • Picking it up stops your sprint, and the Recon super jump is disabled while you carry it.67
  • The Juggernaut can't carry it.8

Unconfirmed

Whether a carrier can sprint again after picking it up is unclear. The client blocks it, but the server's check doesn't mention the ghost. This needs testing in game.

docs.title: Enemy beacons
docs.text:
While the ghost is your active weapon, it boots up for 3.3 seconds and then shows red beacons with distance labels on every living enemy within 45.72 m (1800 units), through walls.9 Your teammates don't see them; spectators watching you do.10

The ghost also beeps faster as the nearest enemy gets closer: every 0.1 × distance in metres seconds, between 1 and 3.5 s.11

docs.title: Being the carrier
docs.text: Everyone else sees a pulsing marker on the ghost or its carrier: red to the enemy, your team colour to friendlies.12 You also get the objective air friction: no bunny-hopping the ghost across the map.13

docs.title: Spawning and dropping
docs.text:
• One ghost spawns each round at a random ghost spawn point.14 With sv_neo_ghost_spawn_bias (on in competitive), rounds play in pairs from the same spawn, so each team gets the same start once.15
  • It drops when the carrier dies or disconnects, or when they press drop while holding it. A dropped ghost is never removed.1617
  • If it's thrown or carried into an out-of-bounds trigger, it's sent back to where the last carrier last stood on solid ground.18

In Juggernaut (JGR), both teams fight over a single JGR56 suit. The player who activates it becomes the Juggernaut: 990 HP, a BALC heat weapon and night vision. While their team has the suit, its kills score points. First team to 20 points wins the round.

docs.title: Winning a round
docs.text:
• A team reaches sv_neo_jgr_max_points (20) team points while the round is live.12
  • Time-out with no living juggernaut, and nobody on the trailing team is mid-activation: the higher team score wins.13
  • Time-out with equal scores and no juggernaut: stalemate.14
  • Time-out while a juggernaut is alive, or while the trailing team is activating the suit: Overtime. Overtime ends when the juggernaut's team is ahead (they win), or when the juggernaut is gone and the first condition applies.15

docs.title: The suit
docs.text:
• Spawns at a juggernaut spawn point each round, and stays locked until 20 seconds after the freeze ends ("JUGGERNAUT ENABLED").16
  • To activate it, hold Use within 150 units for 5 seconds. You're frozen while you hold, and letting go, dying or moving away cancels it.17
  • When you activate it you drop all your weapons, get full health and 100 AUX, and dead teammates are respawned immediately.18
  • When the Juggernaut dies, the suit drops where they fell and can be taken again.19

docs.title: Playing as the Juggernaut
docs.text:
• 990 HP, no bleeding, can't be gibbed.20
  • Only weapon: the BALC, which has no magazine. It overheats after 50 shots, locks for 5 s, and has a charged grenade alt-fire. It doesn't slow you down (×1.0).
  • Can't pick up the ghost or any other weapon.
  • Your position is always shown to everyone on the compass.21
  • Jumps 1.4× higher than normal (50.4 u). AUX regenerates at 10/s.

Unresolved

Juggernaut sprint speed: the per-tick speed code gives 256 u/s, but the defined constant and GetSprintSpeed() say 270. 256 is probably what players get. Not yet checked in game.

docs.title: Team Deathmatch
docs.text: Team Deathmatch (TDM) is a respawn mode. Two teams fight for one long round, and whichever team has the higher score when time runs out wins. The official map is ntre_bullet_tdm.

docs.title: Winning
docs.text:
• When time runs out, the team with the higher team score wins the round.1
  • Equal team scores at time-out: stalemate.2
  • Match ends when a team reaches the score limit in rounds won (default 1, so the first round won ends the match).3

One round

The default score limit is 1 round won, so a TDM match is a single 10.25-minute round.4

VIP is still in development. Its rules and numbers are likely to change, and no official map is built for it yet.

In Extract or Kill the VIP, one team escorts a lightly armed VIP to its extraction zone while the other team tries to kill them. VIP is also the name of the special class the escorted player becomes. The mode uses the same capture zones as CTG.

docs.text:
• VIP escort: the VIP (class NEO_CLASS_VIP) enters the radius of an active capture zone owned by their team (or a neutral zone) while the round is live.1213

docs.title: Damage & penetration
docs.text: Damage in NT;RE is simple: script damage × a global modifier × a hit-location multiplier, reduced only when the bullet passes through a surface. There's no armour, no headshot bonus and no falloff over distance.

docs.title: Damage formula
docs.text:
damage = weapon damage × 1.485 × hit-location multiplier [× penetration loss]12

  • 1.485 is sv_neo_wep_dmg_modifier, applied to every bullet. Explosives use sv_neo_exp_dmg_modifier, also 1.485.3
  • No range falloff. A bullet does the same damage at any distance until it hits something.4
  • Fractional damage carries over. Only whole HP is removed per hit, but the leftover fraction builds up per attacker and is applied once it reaches 1.5
  • No armour. Classes differ only in maximum health: Recon 100, Assault 120, Support 225.6

docs.title: Hit locations
docs.text:
Hit locationDamage multiplierHead×17Chest×18Stomach×0.759Arms×0.7510Legs×0.611

No headshot bonus

NT;RE sets the head multiplier to 1.0, where Half-Life 2 uses 2.0. A headshot does exactly as much damage as a chest shot.

With sv_neo_hitboxgroup_pen 1 (default 0), a shot that hits an arm or leg is traced again to see whether it would also have hit the head, chest or stomach behind it, and uses that multiplier instead.12

docs.title: Penetration
docs.text:
Every gun has a penetration value. When a bullet hits a surface, the game measures how thick it is (up to 12 units) and divides that by the material's value. If the result is no more than the bullet's remaining penetration, the bullet goes through.13

  • Damage after the wall: damage × max(0.25, 1 − used ÷ penetration). A bullet keeps at least 25% of its damage.14
  • The penetration used is subtracted, so the bullet can carry on through further walls with what's left.15
  • Bullets never pass through players.16
  • Shotgun pellets (buckshot) have penetration 0 and never go through anything. The Supa-7 slug does.

Naming trap

The code calls this table PENETRATION_RESISTANCE, but the values work as a divisor: a higher number means the surface is easier to shoot through. Dirt and sand (0.2) are the hardest; glass (0.9) is easy.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text: Movement speed in NT;RE is built up from several multipliers: your class, the weapon in your hands, your stance, and whether you are sprinting or aiming. All speeds are in Hammer units per second (u/s). The base is 2001 u/s, which is Recon's run speed.

docs.title: Speed formula
docs.text:
Each tick, the game recomputes your maximum speed in this order:2

  1. Start from the class run speed: Recon 200, everyone else 160.
  2. Multiply by the active weapon's speed scale (0.675–1.0, see the table below).
  3. Crouching: ×0.75. Walking: ×0.75. The two stack, so a crouch-walk is ×0.5625.
  4. Sprinting: ×1.35 for Recon, ×1.6 for Assault, VIP and Juggernaut. Support can't sprint.
  5. Aiming down sights: ×0.6.
  6. Never below 55 u/s.
  7. For 1.15 s after a jump, every class except Recon is slowed further. The penalty is strongest on landing and fades over that time, with a floor of 75 u/s.

Moving backwards on the ground is scaled by a further ×0.75.3

docs.title: Sprinting
docs.text: Sprinting drains AUX at 5 per second for every class except Recon, and only while you are actually moving.65 You need at least 2 AUX to start sprinting.66 You can't aim while sprinting, and you can't sprint while carrying the ghost.6768

docs.title: Jumping
docs.text: The default jump height is 36 units. Recon jumps 1.5× higher (54 u) and the Juggernaut 1.4× (50.4 u).69 There is no NEO-specific crouch-jump bonus; crouch-jumping follows standard Source behaviour.70 Recon's super jump adds a horizontal boost.

docs.title: Air control
docs.text: In the air, any speed above your normal run speed bleeds away. With the default sv_neo_airfriction 0 nothing is lost, but objective players (the ghost carrier, VIP and Juggernaut) use sv_neo_airfriction_objective 0.5, which stops them from bunny-hopping the objective across the map.71

docs.title: Leaning
docs.text: You can lean while alive, on the ground and not sprinting. Pressing both lean keys cancels the lean.72 Leans are asymmetric: 7.5 units to the left and 15 to the right, to match the original NEOTOKYO. A full lean takes 0.2 s, rolls the camera 20° and lowers your eyes by 2 units.73 Leans are shortened automatically when there's no room.

docs.title: Footsteps
docs.text: Footsteps start at 50 u/s. While walking or aiming, you make no footstep sounds as long as you stay at or below 70% of your class run speed (or of your crouch speed when crouched).74

docs.title: Fall damage
docs.text:
Falls faster than 580 u/s hurt. Damage is (speed − 580) × 100 / 444 × 0.25, about 0.056 HP per u/s over the limit.7576

Note

Because of the 0.25 scale (sv_neo_falldmg_scale), a fall at Source's nominal "fatal" speed of 1024 u/s does only about 25 damage. Damage is linear and uncapped above that.

Thermoptic camouflage (TOC) makes the wearer near-invisible. Recon and Assault have it; Support, the VIP and the Juggernaut don't.6 It runs on its own battery, separate from AUX.

docs.title: Battery
docs.text:
The cloak drains 1 unit per second, applied in whole-second steps, and switches off when the battery drops to 0.1.2 It only recharges while switched off.

Class Capacity Max duration Recharge /s Empty → full Recon 13 13 s 0.55 23.6 s Assault 8 8 s 0.25 32 s

Values from 7.

docs.title: What gives you away
docs.text:
The cloak isn't perfect. Ranked roughly from most to least revealing:

  • Motion vision. Assault motion vision highlights any model moving faster than 0.5 u/s, cloaked or not.8
  • Moving. Each cloaked player has a visibility factor from 0 to 1 that controls how strong the shimmer and tint are. Standing still (≤20 u/s) lowers it by 1.1 per second; moving raises it by speed × 0.004 per second, so about +0.8/s at a full 200 u/s run.910
  • Switching it on. Activation emits a blue light flash (radius 96 units, 0.5 s) and a sound that nearby players can hear.11
  • Firing an unsuppressed weapon causes a 0.1 s flash. Suppressed weapons don't.12

Bots get a bonus to spotting you for a moment after you activate the cloak or fire an unsuppressed weapon.13

Cloaked players and their weapons cast no shadows.14

docs.title: Against thermal vision
docs.text: Support thermal vision draws uncloaked players as hot. A cloaked player is drawn with their normal material and no thermal highlight.15

docs.title: What doesn't break it
docs.text: Only these turn the cloak off: running out of battery, toggling it yourself, dying, or respawning.16 No code switches it off when you fire, take damage or pick up the ghost.

docs.title: Console variables
docs.text: • sv_neo_infinite_cloak (cheat) disables battery drain.17

Every class except the VIP has a toggleable vision mode. Each class gets a different one. Vision modes cost no AUX, have no time limit, and switch off when you die or respawn.1 You can toggle at most once every 0.1 s.2

docs.title: Night vision
docs.text:
Night vision screenshot

Used by the Recon and Juggernaut. It is a full-screen filter only: no entity is drawn differently.3

docs.title: Motion vision
docs.text:
Motion vision screenshot

Used by the Assault. Along with the screen filter, any model whose speed is above 0.5 u/s is drawn again with a highlight material. That includes players, physics props and cloaked players.4 A target that stands completely still isn't highlighted.

docs.text:
Thermal vision screenshot

Used by the Support. Uncloaked players, NPCs, ragdolls and gibs are drawn as hot. The smoke screen overlay is switched off, so Support can see through smoke.56

Cloaked players are not drawn hot. They appear with their normal material, which makes thermal a poor counter to thermoptic camouflage.7
